usage.callShape: POST https://x402.quicknode.com/{network} with JSON-RPC body {jsonrpc,id,method,params} — but only AFTER a one-time SIWE auth handshake to obtain a bearer token, which is then sent on RPC calls
usage.outputShape: body.result (JSON-RPC result), e.g. hex block number — UNVERIFIED (auth wall reached before any RPC executed)
quirks: Price is $10.00 — exceeds the $6 QA hard cap, so it could not be paid in this run. The $10 is a prepaid credit drawdown ($10 USDC = 1M credits), not per-call.
Registry probe reported 402, but live POST calls return HTTP 401 {"error":"invalid_signature","message":"Signature verification failed"} — the real gate is SIWE auth, not a plain x402 paywall.
Requires a one-time SIWE (Sign-In-With-Ethereum) handshake to mint a bearer token BEFORE any RPC call; the bearer token must accompany RPC requests. Plain x402 payment alone does NOT unlock it.
qa-pay --siwx flag did NOT satisfy QuickNode's SIWE flow — still 401 invalid_signature. QuickNode uses its own bespoke auth handshake, not the generic SIWX poller.
{network} path segment must be a real network slug (e.g. ethereum-mainnet, solana-mainnet); supports 79+ EVM/Solana/Aptos networks.
usage.guide: Untested in this run — blocked by two issues. First, the $10.00 price exceeds the $6 QA cap so no payment was made. Second, the endpoint is NOT a plain x402 paywall: live POST calls return HTTP 401 invalid_signature because QuickNode requires a one-time SIWE auth handshake to obtain a bearer token before any JSON-RPC call. To use it, an agent must (1) complete QuickNode's SIWE sign-in to get a bearer token (this also does the $10 prepaid credit drawdown), then (2) POST JSON-RPC bodies like {"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"eth_blockNumber","params":[]} to https://x402.quicknode.com/{network} carrying that bearer token, and read the result from body.result. The generic --siwx path does not work here.
